findings.where: First screen, the photograph of Mark (desktop right half; phone, above the heading)
findings.fault: The direction is 'Mark at work': a full-bleed photograph of him speaking, with his line set over the calm side. Here the lectern photograph has been keyed out of its backdrop and Mark is set as a cut-out head and shoulders on flat slate. Nothing of the event, the lectern or the act of speaking reads. What the visitor sees is a portrait on a dark ground, which is v4's dark ground plus v6's portrait on the right. It is not a photograph of Mark at work.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the first screen first and asked for seven distinct directions. This tile loses its own lever and repeats two others, so it cannot be judged as the 'at work' idea it was briefed to test.

findings.where: Article specimen, the body paragraphs, the subhead and the three-item numbered list (desktop-04, desktop-05, phone-03, phone-04)
findings.fault: The article body is centred, while its title and byline are left-aligned. Every line of long reading starts at a different place. In the numbered list the numbers stay at the left edge and the centred item text drifts away from them: item 2's text starts well to the right of its '2.', and wrapped lines centre under nothing. The list stops reading as a list, and the article has two alignment axes.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader working through one of Mark's articles, which the research calls the product: centred long text is slow to read, and the list falls apart. Angélique too: the specimen is meant to show that the rhythm holds when she adds a list, and here a list is where it breaks.

findings.where: First screen, the scale of Mark's face against the heading and the action (desktop-01)
findings.fault: Set this large, the head fills about two thirds of the screen's height. At a squint, the bright face against dark slate wins over the large serif line and the blue action. The first screen reads like a campaign poster built around a face, not an advisor's considered statement with his photograph beside it.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder, whose brief asks for 'refined, never… salesy or slick' and for his line to come first: here the visitor's eye goes to a close-up face before his words or the way to reach him.

findings.where: Header lockup, 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the MMM Infra logo (desktop-01, phone-01)
findings.fault: The brief's test is that his name leads, with the logo beside it. Here the name is set small and light, and the logo, with its bold white arches, is the bigger and heavier half. At a squint the firm's mark leads and the name trails.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose personal-advisor test comes before craft and fails on 'the firm is the brand'.

findings.where: Phone first screen, the header lockup over the top of Mark's head (phone-01)
findings.fault: The cut-out head rises straight into the header: the logo's arches sit on his hair and the hairline divider almost touches it. The heading then starts at his chin. The lockup, the photograph and the heading are crushed into one stack with no ground between them, so none reads as its own figure.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor arriving from LinkedIn: the first thing they see is the name and logo colliding with a face. It looks crowded and unfinished, the opposite of the calm the direction promises.

findings.where: First screen and the page as a whole: proof of work
findings.fault: Nothing above the fold shows that Mark has done this work: no named body, no event, place or year, and no newest talk. The only dated work, a 2026 lecture, sits at the end of the article specimen, far below. The lede claims whom he advises but gives the reader nothing to check.
findings.who_objects: Staff at a development bank sizing up a consultant, who need to be sure he has done work like theirs for bodies like theirs before they write (first-visit trust items 3, 4 and 13, 'feel the CV'). Only real proof will do; none may be invented.

findings.where: Section labels below the fold: 'PALETTE', 'Type pair', 'Texture', 'An article page', 'Motion sketch'
findings.fault: Five peer sections are labelled four different ways: tracked capitals for PALETTE, small sans for Type pair, An article page and Motion sketch, and a large italic serif for Texture, which therefore outranks its peers. PALETTE's tracked capitals also contradict the type pair's own note, 'never tracked capitals'.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the specimen as the tile's system: labels that disagree with each other and with the tile's own stated rule make it look unresolved.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture card after the article's last line (desktop-05, phone-04)
findings.fault: The card is the only tinted, shadowed, rounded box on an otherwise flat page, and nothing names it, such as 'Related' or 'Lectures'. In the article it outweighs the subhead and the body. Sitting inside the article's column, it reads as part of the article, a promotion dropped into the text, not as the next item in a list of his papers.
findings.who_objects: A reader finishing the article: they cannot tell whether the box belongs to this piece or is a separate item.
